items.text: The documentary "Court of History" was broadcast on Iran International, sparking discussions about transitional justice and punishment of Islamic Republic officials. Some consider execution necessary, while others suggest alternative punishments for rebuilding Iran. Some warned that lack of appropriate punishment could lead to chaos.

A speaker at nightly government gatherings in Tajrish Square, Tehran, said that someone told him there is a smell of burnt meat near the Supreme Leader's residence. He went there himself and confirmed the smell. This claim was made during the gatherings.

The Supreme Court confirmed the death sentence of Arghavan Fallahi, a 24-year-old political prisoner. The sentence was issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Fallahi was arrested on charges of rebellion and was pressured for forced confession.

Fatemeh Jami, an environmental activist, has been held in Gorgan prison for over 53 days without judicial resolution. Her case is under review at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Gorgan, but no hearing has been held yet. This has been confirmed by a source close to her family.

Ali Tajernia, chairman of Esteghlal club, stated that the club will pursue the championship trophy of the past season through FIFA and AFC legal channels and will not give up its rights. He emphasized that the follow-ups are done without political lobbying and that discrimination must end. Tajernia also called the proposal for a three- or five-team tournament a tasteless joke.

Reports indicate a new wave of disciplinary actions at Khajeh Nasir al-Din Tusi University in Tehran. At least 40 students have been summoned to the disciplinary committee. These actions are extensive and recent.

Donald Trump shared a post from American lawyer David Shon stating that Trump gave the Islamic Republic every possible opportunity to change its behavior. Shon wrote that Trump wanted the Islamic Republic to stop supporting global terrorism and join civilized countries. The consequences of continuing the current path were also made clear to the Islamic Republic.

A worker in Delijan was injured due to unsafe working conditions and lack of safety measures. The incident occurred while the worker was performing his duties. The report was published by Harana News Agency.

The Instagram page Ravaq Dar al-Zekr, which published content about the grave of Ali Khamenei and his family members, was blocked by Instagram. This page covered news and images of the burial site of Ali Khamenei and his family members.

The film 'Court of History' by Jamshid Barzegar depicts the history of repression in the Islamic Republic in a condensed case. The film raises questions about how trials should be conducted in Iran after the Islamic Republic. It covers executions, torture, and suppression of protests from the 1980s to the present.

Cristiano Ronaldo returned to the field after more than 240 minutes of absence and scored in the 83rd minute of the Al-Nassr vs Al-Riyadh match. This was his first goal of the season and the 977th goal of his professional career. Ronaldo was the top scorer for Al-Nassr in the last season and missed the first two matches of the new season due to a late arrival.

Donald Trump reshared a post by American lawyer David Shon accusing the leaders of the Islamic Republic of illegal and terrorist behavior. Shon wrote that Trump gave many opportunities to the Islamic Republic to change its behavior, but they did not accept. He also said Trump is now implementing the consequences of the Islamic Republic's continued illegal path.

Shahram Jamali, a resident of Mahmoudabad, was transferred to Amol prison to serve a sentence of seven months and sixteen days. This transfer took place on August 10, 2026. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that increasing the defensive and offensive capabilities of the Islamic Republic must continue rapidly. He described this strategy as the only way to counter current and future enemy actions. Additionally, the production of defense and military products should be accelerated.

French health authorities warned about the sale of tens of thousands of substandard condoms. These products may cause unwanted pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections. An order was issued to recall about 260,000 defective condoms.

Sounds of air defense firing were heard around Yousefabad, Amirabad, and Fatemi. Some believe these sounds are gunfire, while others think they are fireworks related to the "Bayat Eid with Imam Zaman" ceremony. This ceremony was held two days ago at Vali Asr Square in Tehran.

Fars News Agency referred to Pezeshkian's emphasis on ending the war. The agency considers the rhetoric of ending the war as a sign of Iran's weakness. It also stated that the enemy, sensing weakness, launches a stronger attack.

Iran's crude oil loading has dropped to about one-seventh of the pre-war level. China's imports of Iranian oil have also sharply declined to 523,000 barrels per day. Iran's oil reserves in tankers may run out within five months if the current export rate continues.

In the Hat Trick program, Dermot Gallagher, former Premier League referee, reviewed key scenes from the second week of the Premier League. The goal by Malavan against Zob Ahan was correctly disallowed and Amir Reza Afshorde's red card was justified. Also, Shams Azar's penalty and Farshad Mohammadi Mehr's second yellow card were correct.

An official from Iran's Energy Optimization Organization stated that the country faces a daily gasoline deficit of 14 million liters. Daily production is about 115 million liters, but consumption has reached 129 million liters. Additionally, Russia has limited gasoline exports due to domestic needs.

Trump stated that moving towards economic warfare against Iran does not indicate limited military options for the US in the region. He emphasized that the US has full control over the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding land areas. Trump also mentioned that Iran is not yet ready for a proper agreement.

Trump said Iran is willing to reach an agreement but is not yet ready for a proper deal. He added that the US has full control over the area related to the Strait of Hormuz. Regarding US military options, he said they are watching what happens.
Pouria Hosseinifard and Rasoul Rezaei have been sentenced to death. Additionally, Reza Omidvari and Arghavan Fallahi face death sentences. These rulings have been confirmed by the Supreme Court.

The playing style and results of Persepolis in the first two weeks of the Premier League have changed the fans' opinion about Mehdi Tartaar. This issue was explained by Raha Pourbakhsh in the Hat-trick program. The report focuses on the fans' reaction to the coach's performance.

At least three people were injured in a sword attack at a high school in central Sweden. The condition of two of the injured is reported as critical. Police have arrested the attacker, but the motive is still unknown.
CENTCOM announced in a post on X that American forces have changed the course of 68 commercial ships up to 30 Mordad. They also disabled three ships and boarded two.

Trump stated in a speech in South Carolina that the US performance regarding Iran has been as good as with Venezuela. He claimed that the Iranian government is so weakened that no one wants to become its president. Trump also mentioned the US earnings from Venezuela.
Trump stated in a speech in Myrtle Beach that he received the highest votes from homosexuals among Republicans. He also mentioned that he played the national anthem of homosexuals.

Trump warned in a speech in South Carolina that if the Islamic Republic obtains nuclear weapons, it will immediately destroy Israel and the Middle East and likely target the United States. He said that Iran would use nuclear weapons. Trump also mentioned the B-2 bombers and said that a year ago they ended the whole matter.

Chris Wright, the US Secretary of Energy, stated that the US military has helped transfer over 15 million barrels of oil and petroleum products from the Strait of Hormuz. Including pipeline transfers, the total oil leaving the region reaches about 20 million barrels. The seven-day average of oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz is more than eight million barrels per day.

Mike Johnson, Speaker of the US House of Representatives, said the United States is entering a new phase of economic pressure on Iran and that sanctions and economic pressure will be Washington's next step toward Tehran.

Esmail Baghayi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, warned about the dangers of accepting economic sanctions and naval blockade. He emphasized that these actions could lead to the complete erosion of national sovereignty. He also described economic intimidation as an international crime.

Donald Trump stated in his speech in South Carolina that he will not allow Iran to acquire nuclear weapons. He emphasized that once the issue with the Islamic Republic is resolved, oil prices will drop and Iran is eager to reach an agreement. Trump also declared the Strait of Hormuz as American territory and warned about the threats posed by Iran.

Judge Janet Vargas in Manhattan district court struck down the policy suspending immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries. She called the policy "plainly illegal" and beyond the legal authority of Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The policy affected applicants from Latin America, the Balkans, South Asia, Africa, the Middle East and the Caribbean.

Reza Pahlavi criticized the increase in gasoline prices as a result of the incompetence and structural disorder of the Islamic Republic regime. He pointed to fuel smuggling by the IRGC and high consumption of domestic cars. Pahlavi also blamed the car mafia and propaganda apparatus for the fuel problems.

Shayan Samiei said the combination of economic pressure, naval blockade, and military threat has turned pressure on the Islamic Republic into a threat to the regime's survival. He added that Tehran seeks negotiations to buy time. The pressures should continue in a way that negotiation is not an escape route for the regime.

Miad Maleki stated that limiting Iran's exchanges with the UAE blocks one of the main routes for currency supply and imports. He said Tehran cannot rely on China to compensate for this limitation. Beijing is unwilling to risk its economic interests in the US for Iran.

Pegah Bani Hashemi said the December 1404 protests were significant for the Islamic Republic due to their scale and the protesters' determination for change. She identified Reza Pahlavi's role and the presence of a strong alternative as important factors. The protests continue in prisons, with many detainees facing death sentences.

Ghassan Ashour stated that in practice there is no agreement among Shia groups in Iraq for the monopoly of weapons by the government. Some armed groups close to the Islamic Republic still oppose complete disarmament. This opposition indicates that some groups act entirely in line with the interests of the Islamic Republic.

Land subsidence at Parand metro station has again reached a warning stage. Despite measures such as concreting, the phenomenon has intensified. There are concerns about the structural safety of this area.

Donald Trump said that the Islamic Republic lacks money, navy, and air force and cannot pay its forces. He added that the US has full control over the area related to the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also stated that the Islamic Republic is willing to make a deal but has not yet accepted the right agreement.
Manijeh Khoshnoud, a citizen from Bukan, was sentenced to three months in prison by Branch 101 of the Criminal Court Two of this city.

Dalgha Khatinoglu stated that the reduction in Iran's oil loading does not necessarily mean a reduction in exports, as some oil remains in southern Iranian waters due to the US naval blockade. She added that despite oil exports last year, the Islamic Republic faced a currency shortage. Now, with a sharp decline in oil sales and near halt in petroleum product exports, sustaining this situation is difficult.

A video shows that Iranians in Germany held a rally in Dusseldorf on Friday. The gathering was in support of the national revolution and against executions. This event was reported by Iran International.

Ahmad Alavi stated that the Islamic Republic is trapped in a decision paralysis due to corruption, resource shortages, and internal divisions. He said that rising prices could intensify protests. Suppressing protests may deepen divisions within the government.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated at the 'Industry, Mining, and Green Services' conference that the government alone cannot address environmental issues. He emphasized that protecting the environment is a shared responsibility among the government, industry, and the people. These remarks came amid increasing criticism of Iran's environmental policies.

The number of executed prisoners in Isfahan's Dastgerd prison has increased to four. These executions took place in the early hours of Wednesday, August 19. A detailed report on this incident has been published.

Some NATO member countries are considering options to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. This action will not be within the framework of an official NATO mission. Military commanders have discussed possible participation in a virtual meeting.

Mohammad Reza Aref emphasized the need to reform the energy consumption pattern, stating that part of the country's income is spent on gasoline, which imposes pressures on other sectors. He pointed out the difference in fuel consumption between income deciles, noting that the richest decile consumes about 23 to 24 times more than the poorest. Aref linked the opposition of low-income groups to gasoline price increases to their reaction to changes in energy policies.

Iranians in Germany gathered on Friday in front of the Islamic Republic consulate in Munich. The protest was held to oppose executions and repression in Iran. A video of the gathering was sent to Iran International.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said that if unprecedented US sanctions coincide with a large-scale war, the resilience of the Islamic Republic cannot be maintained. He identified the main issue as the fragility of the government.

The regulation for controlled cultivation of Shaqayeq Elifra and the industrial hemp cultivation guideline in Iran have been announced. Cultivation will be supervised and conducted according to the Ministry of Health and Agriculture's regulations. The allowed THC content level defines the legal boundary for hemp cultivation.

The head of nomadic affairs in Semirom reported a shortage of health facilities and difficulties in accessing medical centers for nomads. Drying springs and drinking water supply problems were also mentioned. The possible link between some nomads' health issues and drinking water is under investigation.

Three detainees from the December 2025 protests, Mohammadreza Majidi-Asl, Behrouz Zamani-Nejad, and Kourosh Zamani-Nejad, were transferred from Tehran Grand Prison to Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. The transfer took place on Saturday, August 31. The reason for the transfer is unknown.

The deputy of human resources planning in Kerman's education department announced a shortage of 4,400 teachers for the new school year. Reasons include imbalance between incoming staff and retirements, cancellation of recruitment exams, and lack of soldier-teacher recruitment. Previously, the shortage was reported as 3,000 teachers.

The Public Duty Organization denied rumors about football players serving their military duty in non-military Premier League teams. All athlete conscripts must serve in military sports teams. Alireza Beiranvand will have to serve his military duty in military teams starting from Mehr 1405.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei mentioned the existence of an "octopus" in the automotive industry. He stated that until this "octopus" is removed, the condition and quality of cars will remain the same. These remarks point to structural problems in the automotive industry.

A citizen in Markazi province stated that some people have been forced to steal electric cables due to poverty. This issue was explained in a video sent by him. The incident occurred in neighborhoods of Markazi province.

Reports have emerged about a possible Iranian attack on US positions in Bulgaria. NATO has assured Bulgaria it is ready to defend in case of an attack. Requests have been made to hold a security meeting with the Bulgarian president.

Kayhan newspaper, responding to Ahmad Abedini's criticism, stated that hijab is a necessity of Islam and not a marginal issue. The paper called linking mandatory hijab to economic problems an evasion of religious responsibility. Kayhan emphasized that the government's duty is not only to provide livelihood but also to facilitate the implementation of religious laws.

The street performance of women with optional hijab in Ekbatan has received widespread attention on social media. One user described this movement as the victory of Iranian women against the Islamic Republic. More details are provided in an interview with Ayah Deris.

Farzaneh Fasihi, an Iranian Olympic runner, announced that despite qualifying, she was not allowed to register for the World Championships. She stated that she has been under pressure and was deprived of her basic athlete rights. Fasihi has faced pressure due to her protests against the killings by the Islamic Republic.

Arash Emamjomeh, a citizen from Saqez, was arrested by security forces on Friday, August 14. Nine days after his arrest, there is still no information about his whereabouts or condition. This situation has caused concern.

A video circulated on social media shows Basij forces placing children behind heavy military vehicles. This act is part of the ongoing securitization of the environment. The use of children in military settings has been highlighted.

Kamran Mirhaji, the prosecutor of Fars province, announced that organizers of unauthorized or non-compliant celebrations will be prosecuted. Cafes, halls, and venues hosting such events may be closed. Additionally, related virtual pages and channels will be blocked.

Hossein Taeb warned about the possibility of resuming negotiations and said the Iranian people should not be deceived by the apparent return to talks. He added that the enemy did not fulfill its commitments in the agreement and continued to break promises and apply pressure. These remarks were made at a ceremony honoring mosque activists.

The football360 website owned by Adel Ferdosipour has become accessible again after more than a month of suspension. The site and app were suddenly taken down a month ago, which some linked to Amir Ghalenoei's protests. The national team and related media denied this connection, but Tasnim news agency stated the filtering was due to an interview with Alireza Faghani.

According to a report by Kepler, Iran's oil loading has decreased to 156,000 barrels per day. This amount is about one-tenth of the pre-war level and has made Iran's oil exports disastrous. Continued restrictions may lead to reduced production and long-term damage to oil wells.
A man in Tehran was arrested on charges of assaulting a young woman. After the woman's complaint and the man's confession, he was sent to prison. The case is under judicial authority.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin stated that Trump believes the US will achieve its goals in nuclear, proxy, and missile areas with or without an agreement. He added that the Islamic Republic has become weak in nuclear and proxy areas. Additionally, society no longer equates the Islamic Republic with Iran, indicating the government has lost national authority.

92 percent of participants in the Iran International survey said they do not want to marry or have children due to poverty, insecurity, and an uncertain future. More than 10,000 people participated in this survey. Further details were provided in an interview with Mohsen Mahimini.

A video shows the wife of the missing person Ali Khosravi taking their young child and the deceased wife to his grave. Ali Khosravi was killed by officers on January 8 in Shahin Shahr. His child was born six months after his death.

Asieh Amini stated that the widespread presence of women without mandatory hijab indicates that people have gained the upper hand in the confrontation with the Islamic Republic. She added that the government still holds the law, budget, and tools of repression. This analysis reflects the social situation of women and society.

Participants in a protest rally in Stockholm stated they have not left the streets for eight months. They said they will hold the Lion and Sun flag until Reza Pahlavi calls for action. They also emphasized continuing the path of the families of the disappeared until the fall of the Islamic Republic.

Al Wasl Club of the UAE announced that Mehdi Taremi has joined the team. After years of playing in European football, Taremi has returned to Asian football. Al Wasl will face Shabab Al Ahli in the third week of the UAE league, where Sardar Azmoun and Saeed Ezatolahi play.

Prolonged drought and unprecedented heat have lowered the water levels of the largest reservoirs in the US. Lake Mead has reached its lowest level, and Lake Powell holds only 22% of its water. This situation serves as a warning of the climate crisis in the US.

Arsalan Yazdani, a Bahá'í citizen, was arrested by security forces in Tehran and transferred to an unknown location. His arrest took place on Saturday, 31 Mordad. Some of his personal belongings, including his mobile phone and laptop, were confiscated.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, visited the underground missile production site of the defense industries. He stated that the Ministry of Defense has produced equipment with better quality and quantity. He also emphasized that the enemy cannot fight against the will of the Iranian nation.

Reza Sepahvand, spokesperson for the Energy Commission of the Parliament, confirmed the use of methanol in gasoline blends and stated that the methanol content is about half a percent. He added that this amount does not cause problems for vehicles and claims of damage to car parts are unfounded.

Citizens have installed a joint poster of Prince Reza Pahlavi and his daughter Noor Pahlavi on a street in Tehran. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. The action was reported in Tehran.
Dust storms on the route from Zabol to Zahedan have created a critical situation. Visibility on this route has significantly decreased. This condition has made travel difficult.

Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the IRGC, expressed support for the approach of IRIB and praised its role in the recent war. He described IRIB's performance as valuable in documenting the war's epic and strengthening the Islamic Revolution's media front. This comes after prior criticisms of IRIB's performance by Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Masoud Pezeshkian.

Arzoo Keshvar, owner of a beauty salon in Isfahan, has been sentenced to 12 years in prison on charges of communicating with hostile states. She has been held in Dolatabad prison since last February. After her arrest, she was kept in solitary confinement and subjected to lengthy interrogations.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that messages have been received from neighboring countries regarding new security arrangements and economic cooperation. He accused the US of threatening regional security for Israel's benefit and emphasized the need for a local and independent order. Additionally, the UAE has suspended its commercial activities with Iran until further notice.

Farzaneh Fasihi, an Iranian Olympic runner, stated that she was threatened after protesting the killing of demonstrators in December 2025 and that officials prevented her from participating in the World Championships. She said she was the only Iranian athlete who qualified for the World Championships but was not registered. Fasihi has started legal proceedings to pursue her rights.

In the ninth month of weekly gatherings of Iranians in Stockholm, participants emphasized continuing street presence until the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. Political activists and a performance group called for the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassy in Sweden. The gathering was held to support the people of Iran.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, visited an underground ballistic missile production facility. He was informed about the latest status of indigenous weapons production. Abdollahi emphasized that the enemy cannot fight against the will of the Iranian nation.

Behrouz Safari, head of the Tehran Travel Agencies Association, announced the closure of a large part of travel agencies. The recent war and its consequences have caused nearly two trillion tomans in damages to these offices. Severe market recession and wartime conditions have reduced travel and halted many agencies' activities.

Iranians in Germany held a rally on Saturday in support of the national revolution and against executions by the Islamic Republic in Cologne. This rally was reported through a video received by Iran International.

Mehdi Moslehi, an oil market expert, warned about the low octane gasoline supplied at gas stations. He said using this gasoline can reduce car acceleration, trigger warning lights, and damage parts. This issue can cause serious harm to vehicles.

The sentences of three prisoners related to drug crimes were carried out in Sabzevar prison. These prisoners included Ali Afzali and two brothers named Mostafa and Javad Karabi. The HRANA news agency confirmed their identities.

The Minister of Energy announced that power outages this year are less than last year, but the electricity for agricultural wells was cut for 6 hours a few days ago and now for 8 hours per day. Farmers in Beyza County report their crops are drying up. This issue has raised concerns about electricity management and its impact on agriculture.

The Israeli army announced that Sharif Al-Hasanat, a battalion commander in the Deir al-Balah brigade of Hamas, was killed in an attack. Al-Hasanat was involved in rebuilding the underground network and attacks against Israel. The Israeli army stated that measures were taken to minimize civilian harm before the attack.

Barak Ravid, citing three American officials, reported that on Friday, August 21, about 40 tankers passed through the southern deep route of the Strait of Hormuz. Approximately 16 million barrels of oil were exported through the strait on that day. This information was published on the X network.

Nazar Amidi stated that Iraq will not allow its territory to be used for attacks on other countries. He emphasized that possession of weapons should only be by the government and according to the constitution. He also mentioned the economic and security impacts of the war on Iraq.

Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Sari, was arrested by intelligence officers. The officers entered her home without a judicial warrant and searched it. Personal and electronic items were confiscated from the residence.

Senior African football officials have contacted FIFA Secretary General Matthias Grafström to inquire about his potential candidacy against Gianni Infantino in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Fifteen African federations may not support Infantino. Grafström has not yet taken a clear stance on running.

A citizen protests the poor living conditions by showing the empty refrigerator at home and says people are hungry. He addresses officials, urging them to help. This is a protest against the current economic situation.

Ebrahim Rezaei warned about the presence of American aircraft and refuelers in airports of Qatar, Kuwait, and the UAE, calling it a threat. He cautioned these countries not to complain later. Previously, Ali Abdollahi also warned about the armed forces' oversight of US military activities in the region.
